subject: FinEdge discovery — economics summary and pilot commitment path
messages:
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walsh <sam.walsh@finedge.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:10:00Z
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery call

Sam — thanks for the time today. Quick recap so we're aligned and can move quickly on pilot sizing and commercial ask. High-level notes: 

Pain points we heard
- Real-time reconciliation workload: 60k inference calls/day, spiky at EOD (4x baseline).
- Current latency sensitivity: p95 requirement ~250ms for critical flows; some async flows can tolerate 1–2s.
- Token cost is the single largest line in model infra; procurement has a $75k/year constraint for the initial pilot.

Goals FinEdge set today
- Validate that Redwood can meet p95 latency targets on production-ish load for reconciliation.
- Demonstrate >40% per-token cost reduction on the overnight batch window via batching & prefix caching.
- Produce TCO that shows 12–18 month payback vs current hosted spend.

Levers we discussed (how we'll get there)
- Batching: continuous batching for the overnight window to reduce per-token overhead (estimated 2.5–3x amortization improvement).
- Prefix/KV caching: reuse of common reconciliation prefixes will reduce repeated decoder tokens by an estimated 10–25% depending on hit rate.
- Quantized model variant for non-latency-critical flows (4-bit/INT8) to cut per-token GPU cost.
- Smart routing: keep hot paths on higher-SLA instances, route lower-priority requests to cheaper nodes.

Proposed pilot scope (minimal viable pilot)
- 2-week live pilot: production traffic mirror at 10–20% for reconciliation only.
- Models: full-precision variant for p95-critical paths; quantized medium-latency variant for background jobs.
- Metrics: p95 latency, per-token $ cost, cache hit rate, error/regression rate vs baseline.

Commercial ask / immediate asks
- Target pilot budget: $60k for the 2-week live pilot (covers reserved capacity + engineering support). We can compress to $45k if FinEdge can accept a single region and a strict capacity cap.
- Request from FinEdge: confirmation of budget band, priority of p95 vs cost, and procurement timeline (PO window).

Attachments: FinEdge-Discovery-Slides.pdf (call notes & architecture), FE-TCO-first-pass.xlsx (initial numbers).

Next steps
1) You confirm budget band and procurement ETA.
2) Redwood will run a short cost-sensitivity model and return an updated TCO (v2) with two scenarios within 48 hours.
3) If aligned, we lock dates for the 2-week mirror pilot and share a simple SOW/PO draft.

Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133

----

From: Sam Walsh <sam.walsh@finedge.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finedge.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery call

Monica — thanks for the concise summary, that's exactly what I needed to take internally. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- The $75k/year figure I mentioned is for our initial constrained procurement bucket; for a 2-week pilot we could reallocate up to $50–60k of that, so your $60k ask is within reach but not open-ended.
- Our reconciliation peak happens at 2:00–3:00am PT and the batch window is the most important opportunity for cost savings. If you can show 40%+ improvements specifically there, we'll have a much easier conversation with the CFO.
- Two asks: can you show expected per-token $ at both baseline (no batching) and under the proposed batching/cache settings? Also include an expected p95 delta for the critical path vs our current infra.

I'll confirm procurement timeline next week; procurement wants a 30-day PO window but typically moves faster when we have straightforward SOW/metrics.

Thanks — copying procurement for visibility.

Sam Walsh
Head of Data Products | FinEdge
sam.walsh@finedge.com

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:22:00Z
Subject: RE: FinEdge — pilot sizing suggestion (internal)

Quick internal note after reading the call notes & Sam's reply: 

Suggested pilot configuration (we'll quantify in v2):
- Reserved slice: 1x T4s-equivalent pool for hot path (keeps p95 low), 2x g4dn-like economical nodes for batch/quantized variants during the overnight window.
- Batching targets: 3x effective batch size overnight (expect ~45% token amortization savings), assume 15–20% additional savings from prefix caching.
- If FinEdge can accept single-region (us-west), knock another ~8–12% off the effective infra premium.

Procurement asks: please flag if FinEdge procurement will require SOC2 evidence before PO (Sam said procurement is copied). If yes, we'll attach SOC2 summary + SOC2 point-of-contact.

I'll draft the short SOW template (1 page) we can send once we have budget confirmation.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walsh <sam.walsh@finedge.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finedge.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T14:45:00Z
Subject: FinEdge — updated TCO & next steps (pilot PO path)

Sam — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is FE-TCO-updated-v2.xlsx with two scenarios:

Scenario A — Conservative (single-region, smaller reserved slice)
- 2-week pilot estimate: $48,500
- Expected overnight per-token reduction: ~38% (assumes 3x batching + 12% cache hit)
- p95 on hot path: target ~220–240ms (based on the reserved slice config)

Scenario B — Higher-fidelity (multi-slice for redundancy)
- 2-week pilot estimate: $61,000
- Expected overnight per-token reduction: ~52% (aggressive batching + cache + quantized background)
- p95: target ~200–230ms with extra capacity

Notes: numbers include reserved capacity, engineering support, and observability instrumentation (per-route token breakdown) for the pilot. We did not include long-term enterprise discounts.

Next asks from you to move to PO:
1) Confirm which scenario (A or B) you want to pursue.
2) Procurement: desired PO window (30 days typical) and any required compliance artifacts (I can attach SOC2 summary + encryption/KMS note).
3) Target kickoff dates (we currently have capacity to start a mirror pilot as early as 2027-06-07 if PO confirmed by 2027-05-28).

I've also created a short pilot SOW and linked a HubSpot record for ease of tracking: https://redwood.app/s/FE-2027-0581/hubspot. If helpful, I've dropped a provisional calendar event for a 30-minute pilot kickoff: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=fe-pilot-kickoff

If you confirm via reply, we'll send the one-page SOW and a PO-ready invoice and loop in our Security team for the SOC2 evidence.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133
